Shorter website version
Nikki Adams-Herrera is the founder, owner, and head coach of Cave Training in Santa Clarita and the founder of BabeFit, a prenatal and postpartum fitness and wellness program. With more than 20 years of experience in strength and conditioning, personal training, functional fitness, and women’s wellness, Nikki helps clients build strength, confidence, and sustainable habits through individualized coaching and supportive small-group training. A CrossFit Level 2 Trainer, CrossFit Strongman coach, AFAA personal trainer, BIRTHFIT Coach and Leader, Holistic Nutrition Coach, and doula, she specializes in supporting clients across performance training, general fitness, pregnancy, postpartum recovery, and the motherhood transition.

Motherhood fitness/mental/nutrition support

Motherhood support is a distinct service line, not merely a few workout modifications inside their regular classes. Cave Training’s broader brand offers pregnancy and postpartum fitness, while Nikki’s BabeFit work is specifically designed around prenatal fitness, childbirth preparation, postpartum recovery, pelvic-floor-aware movement, mindset, and community support.

What they offer mothers

Pregnancy fitness

This is strength and conditioning adapted for pregnancy—not simply “lighter workouts.” The goal is to help an expectant mother stay active, build or maintain strength, practice supportive movement patterns, develop breathwork awareness, and train at an appropriate pace as her body changes.

In plain language: safe, coached exercise during pregnancy that prepares a woman for the physical demands of birth and motherhood.

Nikki’s program materials specifically reference movement support, breathwork, pelvic-floor and “womb space” awareness, honoring an individual’s pace, and “soul work” preparation for birth and beyond.

Birth preparation

Nikki is a doula and BIRTHFIT coach, so her offering appears to extend beyond a traditional gym workout. The training is framed around helping mothers feel physically capable, mentally prepared, and supported during the pregnancy-to-birth transition.

Including, fitness and wellness coaching that helps expecting mothers feel stronger, more informed, and more connected as they prepare for childbirth.

This should be positioned as coaching, education, movement, and support—not as obstetric, medical, pelvic-floor-therapy, or rehabilitation services unless a separately licensed clinician is providing those services. Nikki’s materials identify her as a doula, BIRTHFIT coach, and perinatal and pelvic-health coach.

Postpartum fitness

Postpartum training is the process of returning to movement and strength after having a baby, with a focus on recovery, rebuilding confidence, and progressing at an individualized pace. It is generally more intentional than jumping back into standard HIIT, barbell, or boot-camp workouts immediately.

Including, a guided return to fitness after birth, with workouts adjusted to the mother’s current recovery stage, strength, energy, and real-life demands.

BabeFit client testimonials describe support during pregnancy, postpartum recovery, workout modifications, and the ability to bring a new baby while connecting with other mothers. Those are client experiences, rather than a guarantee of individual outcomes, but they show the type of environment the program aims to create.

Pelvic-floor-aware training

The pelvic floor is a group of muscles that supports the bladder, bowel, and uterus. During pregnancy and after birth, people commonly need greater awareness of breathing, pressure management, core control, impact, and exercise selection.

Including, coaching that helps a mother choose and perform exercises more thoughtfully during pregnancy and postpartum, rather than treating her like every other gym member.

Nikki’s Tend(her) course identifies pregnancy/postpartum breathwork and care for the pelvic floor as specific educational areas. This is a meaningful differentiator for her business, especially because standard gym programs often do not address these concerns directly.

Motherhood mindset and community

The offering also has a non-exercise component: helping mothers manage the mental and emotional demands of pregnancy, new motherhood, self-care, changing identity, and isolation. BabeFit’s published mission centers on fitness, community, strength, movement, and connection.

Including, a supportive fitness community for mothers who want to feel less alone while caring for their body and rebuilding confidence.

Non-Pregnant Training options: 

Personal Training — One-on-one coaching. A trainer builds workouts around the person’s goals, teaches proper form, provides accountability, and can adjust training for experience level, injuries, or specific fitness targets.

GPP (General Physical Preparedness) — A small-group, all-around fitness class. It mixes functional movements, strength work, conditioning, weightlifting, and some gymnastics-style bodyweight exercises. Think: “get stronger, fitter, and more capable in everyday life,” rather than training only for one sport. Their GPP sessions are one hour, capped at six people, and designed to be modified for beginners through experienced athletes.

LIFT — A barbell-focused strength class. Members work on movements such as squats, deadlifts, presses, and similar lifts, with coaching on mechanics and technique. It is for someone who wants to build strength, improve form, get more toned, or pursue a heavier personal record safely.

SHRED — A high-intensity interval training, or HIIT, workout. It combines cardio, strength, and conditioning in full-body circuits, including rowing machines and Assault air bikes. This is the class for people who want a challenging sweat, calorie burn, endurance work, and full-body conditioning.

Boxing — Fitness boxing rather than necessarily competitive boxing. It uses heavy-bag drills, punches such as jabs and crosses, core training, conditioning, and endurance work. It suits beginners who want a fun, stress-relieving workout as well as athletes who want to sharpen punching technique and conditioning.

ENDURE — A 40-minute, music-driven cardio circuit. It emphasizes sustained effort and muscle endurance through indoor cycling, rowing, core work, and toning-style movements. This is best described as a high-energy group cardio workout with a strength-endurance element.

Yoga (Restorative Zen Flow) — An occasional pop-up recovery and mobility class. It includes all-levels Vinyasa yoga, breathwork, props, essential oils, and a sound-bath-style restorative finish. It is aimed at flexibility, relaxation, recovery, and overall mind-body wellness after harder workouts.

Nikki Adams-Herrera is not simply a personal trainer or gym owner—she has built a multi-dimensional fitness, wellness, and motherhood-support business serving Santa Clarita through Cave Training and BabeFit. Her work brings together performance coaching, strength and conditioning, small-group fitness, women’s wellness, prenatal and postpartum support, doula-informed care, nutrition-minded coaching, and community-building.
